title: A Signal for the Gravity
premise: Jonah Okonkwo, caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, has spent twelve years hauling cargo through contested orbits to keep the vault alive. When the deep-space vessel Meridian returns with a crew aged backward and memories intact, Jonah shelters them — and learns they carry proof of the Callisto Massacre, an atrocity every archive has been rewritten to erase. As corporate enforcers close in and the crew's reversed biology begins failing, Jonah must choose between destroying the evidence to save their lives or broadcasting it and dooming them. In the end, Jonah seeds the truth into the vault's own genetic archives — hidden inside living plants no one can rewrite — sacrificing their ship and freedom but ensuring justice outlives them all.
about_author: Silas Kavanagh is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for remote Arctic research stations before turning to fiction. He writes slow-burning science fiction about people who maintain things — vaults, ships, truths — long after everyone else has stopped caring.

chapters.title: The Weight of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbits reveals the Meridian drifting silent near the seed vault, its crew biologically younger than when they launched. Jonah, lonely and rule-bound after twelve years of custodianship, makes the fateful choice to dock instead of reporting them. The emotional beat is wary compassion — recognition between two kinds of abandonment.

chapters.title: Records That Dream Otherwise
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Jonah and Meridian's captain, Ilsa Reyes. The crew reveals the Callisto Massacre: two thousand colonists erased, and every official record rewritten while they were in relativistic transit. Their aged-backward bodies are side effects of the drive that let them outrun the cover-up. Enforcer probes begin sweeping the orbit. The beat is mounting dread as loyalty to strangers collides with self-preservation.

chapters.title: Broadcast Zero
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, then Jonah's. With enforcers boarding imminent, the crew debates: transmit the massacre evidence and die, or bury it and live as fugitives. The youngest crew member, aged backward into childhood, begins losing her memories — the reversal erasing the very testimony she carries. Jonah proposes the impossible: encode the truth in the vault's seed genomes. The climax burns with grief and defiance.

chapters.title: What the Earth Remembers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The encoding succeeds as enforcers seize the Meridian; the crew scatters or surrenders, Ilsa staying behind in chains so the transmission window holds. Months later, stripped of his post, Jonah tends greenhouse rows in exile, knowing the truth now grows in wheat and rice worldwide, waiting to be read. The resolution lands on quiet, costly hope: memory kept alive by living things.
